title: Close the switch, the bulb lights
about: A battery, a switch and a bulb are wired in one loop; when the switch closes the loop, the bulb lights.

source.question: What makes the bulb light?
source.answer: Closing the switch makes the loop complete.

story.says: A battery, a switch and a bulb, joined by wires in one loop.
The switch closes, and at once the bulb lights.
The loop is closed all the way round.

shots.intent: The whole loop first: three parts and the wires between them, as close as the three allow.

audit.question: Can a child see a battery, a switch and a bulb joined by wires?

shots.intent: Cause and effect side by side, each as big as the other: the switch in one half, the bulb in the other, one scale, at the same moment, four times slower: the lever comes down, and the bulb comes on.
shots.label: Slow motion: 4 times slower

audit.question: Can a child see the switch's lever come down in one half and, at the same moment, the bulb light up in the other?

shots.intent: Go round the loop the way the current goes, close up, stopping a moment at each part: the bulb, the switch, the battery and back, so 'a complete loop' is something the child has seen all of.

audit.question: Does the camera go all the way round the loop, stopping at the bulb, the switch and the battery?

shots.intent: Back out to the whole lit loop, no wider than the three parts need, and hold.

audit.question: Can a child see the lit bulb, the closed switch and the battery joined in one loop?

notes: The parts sit 0.25 m apart on a large board, so any picture of the whole loop keeps each part small (0.06 to 0.08); the cause and the effect are therefore shown side by side in two halves at one scale, a director's comparison, not the scene's lanes. The travel goes through the parts' centres; the wires droop between them, and the circuits module does not publish their drawn paths yet (DIRECTOR.md 8).
